testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You are braking on dry pavement at 55 mph. How much distance does brake lag add to your total stopping distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: 32 feet
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: If your air compressor has a belt drive, what should you check regularly?
questions.correctAnswerText: That it is properly tightened.
questions.explanation: Check your air compressor drive belt before each trip. Make sure the belt is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: The low pressure warning light comes on while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Exit the road and park as soon as it is safe.
Stop right where you are and park.
Turn on hazard lights and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the road and park as soon as it is safe.
questions.explanation: When the low pressure warning light comes on, safely leave the road and park right away. If air pressure gets too low, your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: What is the most common type of foundation brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: S-cam drum brake
questions.explanation: The most common type of foundation brake is the S-cam drum brake.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensor wires coming from the back of the brakes.
Look under the hood for the ABS sticker.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensor wires coming from the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has ABS, look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires coming from the back of the brakes.

questions.question: What does an air compressor governor control?

options.text: When air is pumped into the air storage tanks
How fast air is pumped into the air storage tanks
The temperature of air pumped into the air storage tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: When air is pumped into the air storage tanks
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when air is pumped into the air storage tanks.

questions.question: What should you do when going down a steep downgrade?

options.text: Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking.
Downshift instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On long or steep downgrades, use engine braking to control your speed. Use your brakes only when you need to.

questions.question: How should you stop during an emergency?

options.text: Veer your trailer to the right and stop.
Veer your trailer to the left and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop in a straight line.
questions.explanation: In an emergency, brake in a way that keeps your vehicle straight. This lets you stop safely and still turn if you need to.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure in the tanks drops below 60 psi?

options.text: A warning light will come on
The vehicle will not shift out of gear

questions.correctAnswerText: A warning light will come on
questions.explanation: When air pressure drops below 60 psi, a low pressure warning signal activates. This can be a warning light or a wig wag.

questions.question: How often should you drain manually operated air tank drains?
questions.correctAnswerText: Every day
questions.explanation: Drain manually operated air tank drains at the end of each day. This prevents oil and water from building up in the tanks.

questions.question: A visual low pressure warning signal should activate before air pressure drops to what level?
questions.correctAnswerText: 55 to 75 psi
questions.explanation: A visual low pressure warning signal must activate before air pressure drops to 55 to 75 psi. This signal can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: Which vehicles must have emergency brakes?
questions.correctAnswerText: Tractors must have them
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must be held by mechanical force.

questions.question: What must all air tanks have?
questions.correctAnswerText: A drain valve
questions.explanation: Air brake system tanks must have drain valves. These valves remove oil and water that build up in the tanks. They can be operated manually or automatically.

questions.question: Why should you drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because old air needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and compressor oil that build up in the tanks and can damage the brake system. Drain the tanks to remove these buildups. Manual drain valves should be drained at the end of each driving day.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.correctAnswerText: May not affect
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the brake pedal

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brake pedal
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. This can damage the brakes by combining spring force with air pressure.

questions.question: What does the air compressor do in an air brake system?

options.text: Pumps air into the air storage tanks
Moves air to the back of the truck

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the air storage tanks
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. The air compressor governor controls the compressor.

questions.question: What should happen before air pressure drops below 55 psi in an air brake system?

options.text: The vehicle will be unable to shift out of gear

questions.correctAnswerText: The warning light should activate
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning signal must activate before the air pressure drops below 55 psi. If the warning signal does not turn on during an inspection, the vehicle is not safe to drive.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning light comes on while driving, what should you know?

options.text: You can only brake if enough air remains in the tanks
You can brake 14 times before the air runs out
You can drive normally and check the brakes later
You can drive with emergency flashers on to warn others

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only brake if enough air remains in the tanks
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning light turns on, stop and park safely as soon as possible. You can only brake as long as enough air remains in the tanks.

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: One brake system with two sets of controls
One brake system for each side of the truck
Two separate brake systems using one set of controls

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate brake systems using one set of controls
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems that share one set of controls. One system typically operates the rear axle brakes. The other system operates the front axle brakes.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, a leak in one system:

options.text: Always means both systems are leaking.
May not affect the other system.
Will also affect the other system.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not affect the other system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other system.

questions.question: Front brake limiting valves were designed to:

options.text: Stop the front tires from skidding.
Stop the front tires from overheating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the front tires from skidding.
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have front brake limiting valves. These valves reduce the risk of front wheels skidding. However, research shows these devices are not needed, so they should be left in the normal position.

questions.question: When operating a vehicle with a dual brake system, a driver should:

options.text: Warm up the vehicle first to get fuel to the engine.
Wait until the air compressor builds at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
Start driving right after the engine starts.
Pump the brake pedal 20 times to build pressure, then drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the air compressor builds at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, let the air compressor build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in:
questions.correctAnswerText: 45 seconds.
questions.explanation: When checking a vehicle with a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems in about 45 seconds.

questions.question: When leaving a vehicle unattended, a driver should:

options.text: Only set the parking brake if parked on a hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always set the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.
